key_insight: Treating the denoising process as a sequential decision problem and using a learned critic to provide dense, per-step feedback lets reinforcement-learning efficiently remove targeted concepts from text-to-image diffusion models while preserving overall image quality.
problem_solved: Removes targeted concepts (e.g., copyrighted or sensitive imagery) from text-to-image diffusion models without heavy supervised weight edits or global penalties, addressing high-variance updates and poor credit assignment typical of sparse, end-of-trajectory RL rewards.
method: Formulate denoising as a sequential decision process where a policy acts at each diffusion step.
Train a critic that provides dense per-step rewards reflecting presence of target concepts and preservation of utility/content.
Use critic-guided RL to update the diffusion policy/controller so outputs avoid the targeted concept while minimizing degradation to image quality and diversity.
impact: Provides a scalable, stable approach for targeted unlearning in generative models, enabling practitioners to remove undesirable concepts with better credit assignment and less quality trade-off — improving safety, compliance, and model maintainability.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: diffusion denoising loop showing policy actions at each step and critic returning dense rewards (feedback loop).
Before/after image grid: sample prompts showing original model outputs vs. outputs after critic-guided unlearning.
Reward timeline: plot comparing sparse terminal reward (high variance) vs. critic-derived dense per-step rewards (lower variance) and resulting training stability.
Tradeoff chart: bars or scatter showing concept removal strength vs. image quality/utility metrics across methods (baseline vs. critic-guided RL).
paper_title: Critic-Guided Reinforcement Unlearning in Text-to-Image Diffusion
paper_authors: Mykola Vysotskyi, Zahar Kohut, Mariia Shpir, Taras Rumezhak, Volodymyr Karpiv
